summary: Report fleet refactoring metrics: publication truth, duplicate clones and lease age

delivery.outcome: monag resume reports per-project and per-checkout fleet refactoring metrics: a publication state that separates dirty work, an ancestry-only delta, a clone with no origin and a missing base; clone identity so parallel clones of one repository are not counted twice; the age of the comparison base so a stale ref is visible; and lease claim age so a dead claim is distinguishable from live work.
nonGoals: Query GitHub or any network service to settle publication state
Fetch, mutate refs, take over a lease or resume any worktree
Change the existing resume schema fields or their meaning
Import GitHub issues into Planfile (reverted deliberately in PR #29)
Track the Planfile store in this ticket: .planfile/** belongs to the integration workstream

architecture.decision: Add a `monag.fleet` module holding the classification and aggregation, and enrich existing `inspect_checkout` rows plus each project with its output. The metrics are additive keys, computed from observations resume already makes, so no new subprocess class and no network access is introduced.
interfaceChanges: monag.resume scan() projects gain an additive `fleet_metrics` object (schema monag.fleet-metrics/v1); checkout rows gain `remote_identity`, `base_ref_age_seconds`, `lease_age_seconds`, `lease_stale` and `publication_state`
architecture.rollback: Revert the ticket commit; the added keys are additive, so any reader ignoring them is unaffected.

validation.evidence: 17 passed; each of the three overcount traps has a pinning test.
128 passed; no regression in the existing suite.

commands: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from monag.resume import scan; scan(Path('<workspace-root>'), depth=2)"
validation.evidence: 69 projects, 141 checkouts, 136 distinct branches, 4 duplicate-clone checkouts, 11 stale lease claims; publication states dirty=81 unmerged_by_ancestry=10 merged_by_ancestry=49 no_remote=1.
